reconciliation.finding: the session-id rule was stated for every seam, but the relay's GET takes sessionId as an optional filter and its answer route uses the opaque question id — a client following the text could reject valid relay calls
reconciliation.change: §1 now separates the two: the team-action routes own the `?sessionId=`-only rule, the relay GET documents the optional filter and the answer route documents the opaque id; both languages changed in the same commit

reconciliation.finding: the panel was described as giving every option a button; it renders only the first question item, at most four buttons, and each tap submits one label
reconciliation.change: §4 states the three limits and the consequence (a multi-item set cannot be answered from the panel because the relay refuses a partial batch); both languages

reconciliation.finding: with no ctx.effect the relay has no lifetime owner and nothing disposes it, yet the boot token still said questions=relay
reconciliation.change: the token gains `lifetime=unowned` and one warning line records it; an owned ctx is byte-identical to before

reconciliation.finding: approveTeam/runDispatch wrapped every failure into { ok:false, error } and the route answered 400 with that text, so a filesystem failure could put a raw path on the wire against the documented generic 500
reconciliation.change: an unexpected throw is marked on the result; the route answers the generic 500 and logs the detail, while an expected policy refusal keeps 400 and its sentence; the TOOL path still rethrows the real sentence

reconciliation.finding: callerForSession and the routes' liveness probe resolve through dsh.liveAgent(sessionId), which matches the AGENT id; a host whose agent id differs from its session id would refuse a live session
reconciliation.change: liveAgentForSession() falls back to a liveAgents() scan matching session.id (the fallback workspaceRootForSession already makes), used by both; the refusal sentence and its position before any store write are unchanged

reconciliation.finding: MAJOR — the two bodies were previously reachable only from a model turn, so calls were serial; now the tool, the service, both routes and a panel tap can run them at once, and two approvals can mint two teams while two dispatch passes can deliver the same task message twice before either CAS rejects
reconciliation.change: an in-process in-flight slot per action, keyed by workspace+sessionId, checked BEFORE the first await and released in finally; a second caller is REFUSED with one sentence rather than queued. Explicit bound: the slot is process-local and does not coordinate two dsh processes

reconciliation.finding: the required dsh-go directory was accepted when it was merely non-empty, so a package carrying some other file and no views/mpd.json passed while the manifest pointed at a missing view
reconciliation.change: the declared view path is READ from the root manifest and required BY NAME in both trees; a new self-test arm reproduces the exact hole (non-empty directory in BOTH trees, declared file absent) and reddens naming the file — 36/36 arms, was 35

reconciliation.finding: a batch answering only some of a parked request's questions settled the whole request, and a single-select question accepted several labels
reconciliation.change: the batch must COVER the request (one entry per item, no duplicates, no foreign ids) and a question without multiSelect accepts at most one label; a refusal settles nothing and the request stays parked for a retry; the panel consequence (it renders the first item only) is documented rather than worked around

bounds: The in-flight slot is process-local: two dsh processes sharing one workspace can still race an approval. Recorded in the code comment and the package README.
